key_insight: The paper builds globally reliable and efficient error estimators for monotone parametric nonlinear PDEs that can also be used directly as loss functions for neural-network surrogates.
engineering_relevance: This gives engineers a principled way to train and validate surrogate models for nonlinear solid/mechanics-style PDEs with guaranteed error control over the full trial space.
method: Split the nonlinear operator into a linear residual plus a strongly monotone closure term.
Measure the linear part in a discrete dual norm and replace the closure’s intractable dual norm with a computable surrogate satisfying pairing and Lipschitz bounds.
Prove two-sided global bounds for both a first-order system least-squares estimator and a discontinuous Petrov-Galerkin estimator.
evidence_signal: The abstract reports theoretical two-sided bounds with explicit constants, verified on a model class of nonlinear fluxes across the stated parameter range.
watch_item: The approach depends on monotonicity and on constructing a computable surrogate for the closure term, so implementation must carefully satisfy the required pairing and Lipschitz assumptions.
paper_title: Global error estimators for parametric monotone nonlinearities and neural approximations
